_note: CI runs every .github/scripts/Tests/*.Tests.ps1 EXCEPT the files listed here.
Adding an entry is how a suite gets skipped; there is no allowlist to forget to update.
EVERY CLASS IS A DECISION ABOUT A SUITE THAT WAS ACTUALLY MEASURED. There is deliberately no class meaning 'not looked at yet'.

class: linux-red    = measured failing on the CI platform. Temporary, so an issue number is REQUIRED. The class says WHERE the failure was observed, not that its cause is platform-specific -- several entries below reproduce on Windows and say so, because this instrument runs only Linux and cannot tell the difference by itself.

class: never-ci     = structurally cannot run in CI, permanently, for a reason nothing in this repository's power removes: a live network or remote-state dependency, an interactive terminal. NOT for an obstacle the gate chooses and could unchoose, such as a checkout depth or an absent token -- that is a decision, and it gets a ticket.

class: no-signal    = the suite executes and yields no verdict at all (every test skipped, or nothing discovered). Resolve-PesterSuiteOutcome treats zero executed tests as not-passed, so promoting one reddens the gate. The condition producing it is expected to end, so an issue number is REQUIRED.

RETIRED by issue #1036: class 'unclassified', which meant the suite's CI-viability had never been measured. 188 entries carried it. Issue #1035 measured the whole corpus on Linux and #1036 spent that measurement, so Get-CISuiteSelection now REFUSES an entry carrying it rather than merely discouraging it -- a class that only shrinks by good intentions does not shrink.

Enforced by .github/scripts/Tests/ci-suite-registration.Tests.ps1, which fails if any suite on disk is neither run nor listed here, and by Get-CISuiteSelection, which fails a class that is not one of the three above, an empty reason, or an issue on linux-red / no-signal that is not a positive integer -- a missing one, or a present-but-unusable placeholder like "TODO", a zero or a negative.

Re-measure with: gh workflow run ci-full-glob-audit.yml --ref <branch>. The --ref is load-bearing; without it you measure the default branch. That workflow is RED BY CONSTRUCTION (it ignores this registry), so read the per-suite record on issue #1035 rather than the job's conclusion.

Readings of structural suites against specific delivered trees are collected in Documents/Design/test-suite-baseline-948.md; see its section on the promotion tranche (issue #1050) for what composite-skill-structure.Tests.ps1 reports today and why that result is a constant rather than a signal. That suite is no longer quarantined -- issue #1036 promoted it -- so it runs on every pull request; its result being a constant is a property of the suite, not of its gating.

quarantine.reason: Measured failing on Linux in every audit run, most recently 31439187268 at 1f9afb5 (126 executed, 1 skipped). READ THE CLASS NAME CAREFULLY: it records where the failure was OBSERVED, and this instrument runs only Linux, so it cannot itself tell a platform defect from a locale one. This is the latter. `skills/calibration-pipeline/scripts/aggregate-review-scores-core.ps1` renders percentages with `'{0:P0}' -f`, which formats using the CURRENT THREAD CULTURE: en-US puts no space before the sign ("80%") and the invariant culture does ("80 %"), and an unlocalised Linux container resolves to invariant. The suite passes on Windows, 126 passed and 1 skipped at 1f9afb5, only because the dev host is en-US — it would fail on a Windows runner with no locale too. Ends when the renderer formats through a fixed culture rather than the ambient one.

Measured failing on Linux in every audit run, most recently 31439187268 at 1f9afb5 (19 executed). The suite builds a `gh` stand-in on PATH as `gh.cmd`; Windows resolves a bare `gh` to it through PATHEXT, Linux has neither extension matching nor an execute bit on that file, so resolution falls through to the runner's real `/usr/bin/gh` — and the suite's own assertion says so, reporting `/usr/bin/gh` where it expected the shim path. Passes on Windows, 19 of 19 at 1f9afb5, for exactly that reason. Ends when the shim factory writes an extension-less executable file on non-Windows. ONE ROOT CAUSE, THREE SUITES: shared with post-merge-cleanup.Tests.ps1 and session-startup-git-helpers.Tests.ps1, which is why one issue is cited three times rather than three issues filed for one defect.

Measured failing on Linux in audit run 31439187268 at 1f9afb5 (14 executed). It was GREEN in the two runs before that with a byte-identical content digest (c1d3590bcf84) — nothing in the suite changed, so the cause is outside it. The failing test resolves the merge-base of `main` and `HEAD` in the live repository as a deliberate non-mocked sanity check; this workflow and the per-PR gate both check out with a bare `actions/checkout`, which is fetch-depth 1 and no local `main` branch, so there is no merge-base to resolve. NOT `never-ci`, deliberately: a checkout depth is an obstacle the gate CHOOSES and could unchoose, which makes it a decision rather than a structure. Passes on Windows, 14 of 14 at 1f9afb5, where a full clone exists. Ends when the gate fetches enough history, or the test skips itself when no local main is present.

Measured failing on Linux in every audit run, most recently 31439187268 at 1f9afb5 (13 executed). Not a platform defect: the suite runs real `git init`, `git commit` and `git worktree add` and never checks their exit codes, and `git commit` requires a configured identity that NEITHER this workflow NOR the per-PR gate supplies — the audit's own environment statement records `git identity: none configured` on both sides. It passes on Windows, 13 of 13 at 1f9afb5, only because a maintainer's machine carries a global identity; a fresh Windows runner would fail it too. Ends when the fixture sets a repo-local identity and surfaces failures of its own setup commands instead of swallowing them into misleading downstream assertions.

Measured failing on Linux in every audit run, most recently 31439187268 at 1f9afb5 (50 executed). Same root cause as migrate-brief-review-corpus.Tests.ps1: the suite's `gh` stand-in is written as `gh.ps1` plus `gh.cmd`, neither of which Linux resolves for a bare `gh`, so `Invoke-SCDGhWithTimeout` reaches the runner's real gh, gets a non-zero exit, and collapses it to the catch-all `gh unavailable` — which is what the failing assertions report in place of the answer the mock was configured to give. Passes on Windows, 50 of 50 at 1f9afb5. Ends with the same fix, under the same issue.

Measured failing on Linux in every audit run, most recently 31439187268 at 1f9afb5 (69 executed). The suite's git and gh stand-ins are written as `git.cmd`/`git.ps1` and `gh.cmd`; Linux resolves none of them for a bare command name, so the detector runs the runner's REAL git against non-repository fixture directories, takes its fail-open branch and emits nothing — after which the harness binds that empty string to a mandatory `[string]` parameter and throws. Passes on Windows, 69 of 69 at 1f9afb5. #904 predates any measurement and describes the symptom ("detector under-reports on Linux"); the mechanism above is what the audit now shows, and the same shim defect affects three other suites. Kept on #904 rather than folded into that issue because #904 is this suite's own ticket and the parent chunk requires it stay tracked here.
